subject: ApexHealth deployment isolation alignment & canary plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morrison <alice@apexhealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@apexhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-12T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: ApexHealth deployment isolation alignment & canary plan

Hi Alice / Procurement team —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Wanted to capture the short recap and the decision points we discussed so we have clear next steps. High-level call notes below, plus an initial canary plan we can run in parallel with procurement.

Call highlights
- Primary concern: strict data separation and custodian controls for PHI-derived inputs.
- Ops team leaning toward a Private VPC or on-prem control plane due to audit requirements; application team prefers Dedicated for lower operational overhead.
- Key gating items: KMS integration, audit log retention (7 years listed), privileged access controls, and evidence for network isolation.

Questions / clarifications we agreed to resolve
1) Which customer-managed KMS (cloud provider & key rotation policy) do you need for the control plane? (you mentioned an existing Key Vault in GCP)
2) Do you require inbound-only egress filtering from the inference hosts (i.e., block control plane egress to unknown URLs)?
3) Is there a hard requirement for on-prem data residency for any production routes, or is a VPC in your cloud tenancy acceptable?

Proposed canary approach (minimal disruption)
- Phase A (Dedicated pool): deploy a small Dedicated capacity pool with model pinned to v1.0, restrict runbooks and generate audit evidence for a week.
- Phase B (Private VPC pilot): deploy control plane into your VPC with KMS integration and restricted subnet routes; run identical traffic patterns.
- Success criteria: identical latency envelope within +20% and evidence of required logs/KMS operations available to your security contact.

Attachments: redwood-deploy-checklist.pdf (PDF, 48KB) — initial checklist we’ll use to capture evidence; apex-q3-security-asks.xlsx (XLSX, 12KB) — security gating items you shared.

Next steps
- Alice: confirm the KMS provider and whether the security team requires absolute on-prem residency or a customer VPC (reply by EOD Tue).
- Procurement: if Dedicated is acceptable as an interim option, we’ll share a 30-day reserved capacity quote and can start Phase A once mutual NDAs are in place.
- Jordan/Marissa: we’ll draft the canary runbook and security evidence template for your review.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan@redwood.com] | +1 415-555-0123

From: Alice Morrison <alice@apexhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@apexhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-13T09:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ApexHealth deployment isolation alignment & canary plan

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few quick answers from Security/IT: 

- KMS: we run keys in GCP KMS (projects: apex-prod-keys). Rotation policy is 90 days, and we will require an attestation that Redwood can integrate with our CMEK keys for the control plane.
- Egress: we need strict egress allow-lists from inference hosts; anything outside our approved endpoints should be blocked.
- Residency: VPC (in our AWS tenancy) will be fine for now — on-prem is not mandated for prod, but we do require the VPC to be under our account and have private routing to our audit sys.

On the canary plan: Procurement is fine with a short Dedicated pilot while security completes the VPC onboarding. For procurement we’ll need: 
- A short-term committed quote (30 days minimum) showing unit pricing and cancellation terms
- Basic SLA terms for latency and availability for the pilot
- Confirmation that audit logs and KMS operation logs will be accessible during the pilot

I’ll share a consolidated list from Security by tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Alice Morrison
Head of IT Security | ApexHealth
alice@apexhealth.com | +1 617-555-0789

Alice —

Perfect, thanks for the quick clarifications. I pulled Kimberly into this thread to own the security evidence and KMS integration plan on our side. Short note on next concrete actions so procurement and security have owners and timelines: 

Action owners & timeline
- Redwood (Kimberly): produce KMS integration design doc for GCP CMEK + auditing expectations; include sample log retention queries. Target: 2028-09-18 EOD.
- Redwood (Jordan + Marissa): deliver a 30-day Dedicated pilot quote and pilot SLA doc. Target: 2028-09-15 EOD.
- Apex (Alice): send consolidated security requirements and point-of-contact for VPC onboarding. Target: 2028-09-15 morning.
- Procurement (procurement@apexhealth.com): ack receipt of quote and advise on PO timelines once quote is received.

Pilot acceptance criteria (short list)
- KMS operations are visible to Apex security (proof: sample log export and KMS op IDs).
- Audit logs show separated tenant IDs and are exportable to Apex’s SIEM.
- Performance: 95th percentile latency delta vs current baseline <= +20%.

We’ll attach the runbook and the checklist referenced earlier once Kimberly sends the KMS doc. Would you like a short 30-minute working session this week to walk through the KMS flows and VPC peering steps? I’m available Thu 10:00-11:30 PT or Fri 13:00-15:00 PT.

Thanks again — looking forward to moving the pilot forward.

Jordan Blake
